messages:
maria_customer: Hey team — running into a weird issue with our SSE streaming integration. Client starts a stream, we get partial text events for ~30s, then the connection stays open but no more events. After a minute client re-connects and finishes, but billing shows double tokens for the same prompt. Any idea?

alex_support: Sorry you're hitting that, @maria_customer. Can you share the request headers (redact keys) and the approximate times? Also whether you're reconnecting manually or the client auto-retries.

maria_customer: Auto-retry in the browser (EventSource) with a 3s backoff. First request 2026-11-03T14:12:45Z, then reconnect at 14:13:18Z. Authorization header has a short-lived token (rotated by our auth proxy). We pass a client-id and session-id in the query params.

alex_support: Thanks. Two quick hypotheses: 1) a mid-stream 429 from our rate limiter caused the server to stop sending events but not close the socket (so client sees silence), then the client retried and triggered a second billing window; or 2) token rotation caused the reconnect to be treated as a new stream and the two partial outputs were both charged.

jamie_sre: Jumping in. Can you paste the last 3 lines of the client console network trace (sensitive bits redacted)? Also, do you have any server-side logs showing 429 or auth failures at those times?

maria_customer: Console shows EventSource connected -> a few "data:" events -> then long silence. No explicit close. Network tab shows the SSE connection as "200 OK (pending)" during the silence. After reconnect, new EventSource gets 200 and more events. No 4xx on the wire.

alex_support: Interesting — on the wire no 429, but billing says two charges. Kendrick / billing, could token accounting ever count partial stream tokens twice if the connection stays open and a reconnect succeeds?

kendrick_billing: We typically attribute tokens to the request that completes on our backend. However, streaming has a tricky path: we increment 'tokens_billed' on each chunk flush and mark a request as settled on connection close or final event. If a reconnect results in the same logical prompt being resumed, we try to reconcile via session id, but that only works if the session id matches and the reconnect flow includes an idempotency header.

jamie_sre: Can we check infra logs for the device timestamps? I'm seeing an anomaly in the gateway logs: connection at 14:12:45 from ip 54.23.9.1, no 429 responses, but the stream handler logged a transient internal: "kv-cache-miss -> batch-evict" at 14:13:16 which coincides with the silence. There's also an entry: "stream-heartbeat: missed 3 pings, marking stalled but not closing"

alex_support: So the server marked the stream stalled and stopped sending more events but didn't close the connection. The client sees an open pending socket and doesn't consider it failed. When it finally reconnected, the resumed work ran a new inference on the backend, which produced additional tokens billed. That could explain double billing.

maria_customer: That matches our experience. Is there an expected behavior — should a stalled stream be closed with a 429 or 5xx so clients auto-retry sooner?

jamie_sre: We shouldn't be sending 429 mid-stream. 429 is rate-limiter-triggered and normally returned by the gateway at request acceptance time. Mid-stream 429s are a symptom of the per-connection quota check kicking in asynchronously when usage spikes. Our gateway has logic that can short-circuit an in-flight stream when the tenant exceeds burst quotas, but it should close the connection with a 429 event and a termination frame. The log above shows we marked it as "stalled" due to KV cache eviction impacting runtime rather than an explicit quota rejection. That path currently doesn't emit an outbound SSE close with an error frame — bug.

alex_support: So two problems: 1) stall path doesn't close with an error frame -> clients hold open; 2) reconnects treated as new requests without strict idempotency -> double charge. Proposed short-term mitigations: a) update gateway to emit well-formed SSE error frame and close connection on quota/stall; b) in billing, apply a reconciliation heuristic to detect likely duplicate partial streams within short time windows by session-id + prompt-hash and credit duplicates.

kendrick_billing: We can push a reconciliation job to detect duplicates where two distinct request-ids have overlapping token footprints and identical session/prompt within a 5-minute window. I can prod that as an emergency refund path for affected accounts.

jamie_sre: For a fix, I'll open an incident PR to change the stall handler to: emit `event: error\ndata: {"code":429,"reason":"quota_or_runtime_stall"}` then `event: close` and close the socket. Also add a metric for "stalled_streams_closed" and roll this to prod (hotfix, low risk) and follow-up to add an idempotency header for streams.

maria_customer: Would adding an idempotency-key on the client help immediately? Our EventSource implementation can't set headers easily. We can move to fetch+stream with Authorization and custom headers if that's the recommended path.

alex_support: Yes, fetch streaming with a Retry-Id header (UUID per logical prompt) is the more robust recommendation. EventSource doesn't allow custom headers so it's awkward for auth rotation and idempotency. We'll document it in the short term and include a sample snippet.

alex_support: Sample repro steps I want to record here so others can reproduce: 1) Start a long-running SSE generation via fetch or EventSource; 2) Simulate KV-cache eviction by sending many concurrent short requests from same tenant to force runtime pressure; 3) Observe that mid-stream the runtime logs a "stalled" event without outbound close; 4) Client reconnects and receives additional tokens; 5) Billing shows two charges.

jamie_sre: Adding logs to reproduce: gateway logs (redacted):
```
[2026-11-03T14:13:16Z] gateway: conn=abcd1234 tenant=acme001 handler=stream start
[2026-11-03T14:13:16Z] runtime: kv-cache-miss: model=v2 seq=1024 -> evict batch
[2026-11-03T14:13:16Z] runtime: stall-detected conn=abcd1234 reason=kv-pressure
[2026-11-03T14:13:16Z] gateway: stall-handler: marked_stalled conn=abcd1234
```

jamie_sre: After the hotfix we'll expect logs like:
```
[2026-11-03T14:13:16Z] gateway: stall-handler: emitting_error conn=abcd1234 code=429 reason=quota_or_runtime_stall
[2026-11-03T14:13:16Z] gateway: stall-handler: close conn=abcd1234
```

alex_support: Action items:
- jamie_sre: open PR to emit SSE error+close and add metric, target rollout to prod in next 2h. (high)
- kendrick_billing: run duplicate-charge detection for tenant acme001 and prepare refunds for matches. (high)
- alex_support: update docs with fetch+stream sample using X-Idempotency-Key and recommend server-side session-id binding. (med)
- maria_customer: if possible switch to fetch+stream or add session id in query param and report back results. (low)

kendrick_billing: I'll also check if the billing pipeline already merged both partial token tallies into one billing event. If not, we'll create a refund queue and contact ops to prioritize.

maria_customer: Thanks all — will try switching to fetch+stream this afternoon and report. Appreciate the quick triage.

deploy-bot: deploy job #3821 started for gateway hotfix -> rolling to canary (us-west-2).

jamie_sre: Canary looks good (no regressions observed), metric "stalled_streams_closed" incremented 7x during canary -> indicates the fix is catching previous silent stalls. Rolling to prod now.

alex_support: Kendrick, let us know when refunds queued and if you need a list of affected request IDs.

kendrick_billing: Will do. Estimated remediation timeline: refunds queued within 24h; docs + sample code in 48h.

maria_customer: Confirmed after switching to fetch+stream with an idempotency key we no longer saw duplicate billing and the client retried cleanly when we forced a stall. Great work! :tada: 

alex_support: Closing thread once refunds confirmed. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround."
